Such journals are labeled \u201cpredatory\u201d journals. This study examines author profiles for some of these \u201cpredatory\u201d journals as well as for groups of more well\u2010recognized open access journals. We collect and analyze the publication record, citation count, and geographic location of authors from the various groups of journals. Statistical analyses verify that each group of journals has a distinct author population. Those who publish in \u201cpredatory\u201d journals are, for the most part, young and inexperienced researchers from developing countries. We believe that economic and sociocultural conditions in these developing countries have contributed to the differences found in authorship between \u201cpredatory\u201d and \u201cnonpredatory\u201d
